samples.summary: Three gates now hard-depend on `github.event.workflow_run.path` with no fallback; if that field is ever empty in the payload the panel, the CI-fix arm and ci-report all go permanently inert, silently
samples.evidence: `agent-review-panel.yml:166`, `agent-iterate-ci.yml:54` and `ci-report.yml:56` each add `github.event.workflow_run.path == '.github/workflows/ci.yml'` to the gating job's `if:`. GitHub expression semantics make an absent/empty property compare false, so if `path` is not populated on a `workflow_run` payload (notably the `requested` action, which is the event that STARTS the panel) every one of these gates evaluates false. The failure is invisible: the `gate` job is skipped, so `stalled` (which needs `gate.outputs.managed == 'true'`) never fires, and the concurrency suffix independently routes such runs to the `noop` lane — no page, no comment, no red check. The only verification is `checks.test.mjs`, which feeds the expression synthetic PATH values rather than a real payload, so it cannot detect the field being absent. The blast radius is the entire autonomous loop plus PR CI reporting. I could not confirm from the repo that `path` is present on `workflow_run.requested` payloads, hence low confidence, but there is no fallback (e.g. also accepting `github.event.workflow.path`) and no alarm if the assumption is wrong.

samples.summary: The YAML path gates use exact `==` while `ciRunsFor` deliberately strips an `@ref` suffix — the same identity check is implemented two different ways
samples.evidence: `checks.mjs:62` compares `String(r?.path ?? "").split("@")[0]` precisely because "called workflows report `path` with an `@ref` suffix", and `checks.test.mjs:487` / `mark-ready.test.mjs:251` pin that tolerance. The three workflow gates added by the same change (`agent-review-panel.yml:117` and `:166`, `agent-iterate-ci.yml:54`, `ci-report.yml:56`) compare with a bare `==` and cannot tolerate the suffix. If the suffix ever appears on the triggering run's payload (the case checks.mjs says it must handle), mark-ready's gate 1 keeps passing while the panel refuses to run at all — the divergence is silent in the direction that disables the pipeline, and the concurrency suffix at line 117 would simultaneously push such runs into the `noop` lane. Either both should strip the suffix or checks.mjs's tolerance is dead code; today they disagree.

samples.summary: `ciConclusion` requiring EVERY run for the SHA to be green creates a state no remediation path can clear: `@claude rerun` re-runs only the newest run (`per_page: 1`)
samples.evidence: `ciConclusion` (checks.mjs:84-89) returns `"failure"` if any run of ci.yml for the head SHA is non-success, so a single stale red/cancelled run pins gate 1 red for that SHA forever. The recovery mechanism does not cover it: `agent-rerun.yml:187` and `agent-loop.yml:143` both call `listWorkflowRuns({ workflow_id: 'ci.yml', head_sha, per_page: 1 })` and `reRunWorkflow` on that single newest run. Re-running the newest run leaves the older red run untouched, so `ciConclusion` still says `failure`, promote exits 1 → "gates unsatisfied", the job SUCCEEDS, nothing pages, and the PR stays a draft indefinitely — exactly the stall the promote job's own header comment says it exists to prevent. Reachable today via PR close/reopen (`pull_request` default types include `reopened`, which creates a second run for the same head SHA) and by construction the moment CI gains a second trigger for one commit, which the function's own docstring anticipates.

samples.summary: Behavior regression for a SHA carrying an old non-success run plus a newer green one: previously promotable, now permanently blocked
samples.evidence: The old `ciPassed` sorted newest-first and read `runs[0].conclusion`, so a superseded `cancelled`/`failure` run followed by a fresh green run promoted. `ciConclusion` (checks.mjs:86-88) now returns `failure` for that same input (pinned by mark-ready.test.mjs:265-280). The fail-closed direction is intentional, but the consequence is not bounded: a blocked gate 1 means exit 1 → the promote job succeeds with "leaving as draft", and nothing re-runs the panel for that SHA, so the PR is stuck until a human pushes a new commit. The change also treats `cancelled`, `timed_out`, `neutral` and `skipped` identically to `failure` with no way to distinguish "CI was cancelled" from "CI failed" in the loop-status note.

samples.summary: `workflow_id: 'ci.yml'` is duplicated in two workflows and is not covered by the new CI_WORKFLOW_PATH existence test
samples.evidence: The change introduces `CI_WORKFLOW_PATH` plus a test (`checks.test.mjs:447`) asserting the file exists, precisely because "a typo, or renaming ci.yml, silently makes the gate unsatisfiable". Two other places identify CI by the same filename and are not covered: `agent-rerun.yml:187` and `agent-loop.yml:143` (`workflow_id: 'ci.yml'`). Renaming ci.yml would leave those two lookups throwing/empty — both are wrapped in `catch` and degrade to "the loop will engage on the next CI run", so the breakage is silent, while the new test would still pass or fail elsewhere. Nothing pins these literals to the constant.

verdict.reason: The three path clauses exist exactly as quoted (agent-review-panel.yml:164-169, agent-iterate-ci.yml:52-56, ci-report.yml:54-56), and the silent-skip mechanics (stalled keying on gate.outputs.managed, agent-review-panel.yml:2322-2331) are read correctly. But the finding's premise — that `github.event.workflow_run.path` may be absent/empty, notably on the `requested` action — does not hold, and the reviewer concedes it is unverified. `path` is a property of the workflow-run resource itself, populated at creation; only lifecycle fields like `conclusion` are null at `requested`. The same gate already reads `run_attempt` and `head_repository.full_name` off that identical object on `requested` events (agent-review-panel.yml:167-169), so a sparsely-populated `requested` payload would already have broken the pre-existing clauses. The repo also already depends on this very field in production for the promotion gate: checks.mjs:58-62 filters CI runs on `r.path` and mark-ready.mjs:135-138 consumes it, with checks.test.mjs:443-453 guarding it — an empty `path` would have made promotion permanently unsatisfiable long before this change. The `@ref`-suffix case that checks.mjs:60 strips cannot reach these gates either: ci.yml:4-28 is a top-level workflow (push/pull_request/merge_group, no workflow_call), so its runs report a plain unsuffixed path, and the strict `==` matches. What remains is a defence-in-depth request (add a fallback / add an alarm) against a failure mode with no demonstrated mechanism, where the current behaviour fails closed by design (harness-engineering.md:1931-1949) — at most nit-grade under the Correctness rubric, not a blocking logic defect.
